answer: Route every payment through a shared lagoon: funds entering the economy settle not instantly but at the next network pulse, a fixed-interval settlement where a random sample of the pending river of transactions is audited by bonded strangers. A sybil farm can mint a thousand identities, but each one's money sits in the same lagoon, exposed to the same audit lottery — one caught puppet forfeits its whole batch, and the farm must fund every clone's escrow separately while waiting out each pulse. Honest agents barely notice the delay; attackers pay it on every fake identity, every cycle.
